question.question: After an implicit joint change is fully applied but its automatic leave proposal is dropped during a leadership transfer, does transfer timeout leave a stable healthy leader without any implementation-owned continuation to exit joint state?
question.importance: A permanently retained outgoing quorum can prevent subsequent reconfiguration and retain dependence on members intended to leave. This concerns automatic continuation, not a numeric response deadline.
contexts: Implicit joint transition; synchronous apply-before-Advance; transient transfer-message loss followed by healthy delivery; no additional client proposals
event_paths: Commit joint entry -> apply configuration -> start transfer -> Advance final committed batch -> automatic leave rejected -> transfer timeout -> ordinary Tick/Ready/network processing

supporting_behavior_ids.B-context: Transfer excludes proposals until timeout clears transferee without scheduling appliedTo.
supporting_behavior_ids.B-proposal: Proposal admission drops work during transfer; subsequent commit could generate another application completion.
supporting_behavior_ids.B-ready: Provides application completion and ensures no owed Ready is skipped.

counterevidence: Ordinary application completion without transfer proposes leave immediately.
A later application completion retries, and a new leader appends a new-term entry that can supply one.
No numeric deadline is specified; a finite absence alone cannot establish failure.
unknowns: Can a legal drained schedule enter a repeatable full protocol-state cycle after transfer failure while AutoLeave remains true?
question.trigger_rationale: The public implicit-transition and tracker contracts assign departure to Raft when possible. The source names application as the retry trigger but the timeout clears only transfer state. A controlled drained schedule can distinguish a lost trigger from an independently scheduled retry; simple additional timer variants would not.

obligation.description: For an implicit joint configuration assigned to Raft, after its entry has been applied and a transient leadership-transfer attempt has ended, a stable eligible leader with available joint quorums must retain an automatic path to propose leaving joint state. It must not remain in a closed repeating protocol execution with AutoLeave set and no leave proposal solely because the last application-triggered attempt was rejected during transfer.

scope.description: Automatic continuation of implicit joint exit under a stable leader after failed transfer, with all emitted storage/application work completed and ordinary ticking/message delivery continued.
assumptions: Non-Byzantine participants and valid initial configuration.
Synchronous caller persists before sends, applies entries/configurations before Advance, and processes all emitted work in order.
Transfer attempt may lose a TimeoutNow; after timeout the suffix delivers all network traffic and ticks every node.
No independent new client proposal or manual leave-joint is owed.
excluded: A fixed elapsed-time or tick deadline for leaving joint.
External client read completion or whole-cluster safety violation.
Schedules with missing application completion, unavailable quorum, leadership change or explicit joint mode.

grounding.derivation: ConfChangeTransitionJointImplicit explicitly assigns automatic transition by a zero configuration proposal; Config.AutoLeave says Raft owns transition when possible. appliedTo initiates that proposal but the transfer guard may reject it. A closed repeatable healthy suffix with no emitted leave proposal would refute automatic continuation without inventing a deadline; finite noncompletion without recurrence would remain unknown.
grounding.applicability: Implicit joint mode with completion of the entering entry, transfer no longer active, and all ordinary protocol/application duties served.
unresolved: The proposed recurrence observation must account for all behavior-determining state, queued messages, timers, callbacks and caller work.
alternatives: Later client work or a leadership change could rescue the transition, but those are separate stimuli and are not used to define automatic continuation under the stable suffix.
